messages:
maya-support: Escalation from ACME — multiple customers reporting 502s on hosted API (/v1/generate and /v1/embeddings) starting ~2024-10-12T09:12:00Z. Customer says errors spike during batched requests. Attaching sample trace id: trace=acme-9f3b.
jon-eng-sre: Thanks — are these primarily 502 or 504? any upstream error codes in traces?
maya-support: Mostly 502, occasional 504s. Sample trace shows edge returned 502 after fanout to auth service returned 500. Excerpt from edge log: ```[2024-10-12T09:12:14Z] trace=acme-9f3b route=/v1/generate method=POST status=502 upstream_status=500 upstream="auth-tenant-lookup" fanout=6 headers=[Authorization, x-tenant-id, x-request-id] msg="upstream error: unknown tenant"```
alex-platform: Observed a jump in concurrent fanout for that route ~09:11-09:15 UTC. Many requests are batching embeddings and we see ~5-8 parallel auth lookup calls per request. Auth cache miss rate up ~18% -> backend stressed. Also noticed some requests carry duplicate tenant headers (both X-Tenant-ID and x-tenant-id) which the backend treats differently, causing lookup failures.
kai-oncall: Can we reproduce locally with a small curl? maya-support can you paste a repro?
maya-support: Repro that customer ran:
```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Tenant-ID: 12345" -H "x-tenant-id: 12345" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
* Connected to api.redwood.ai
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
< {
  "error": "edge: upstream returned 500 during fanout to auth-tenant-lookup",
  "trace": "acme-9f3b"
}
```
This pattern (duplicate header casing) seems to trigger auth service path that misses the canonical tenant and raises a 500.
jon-eng-sre: That makes sense — our auth microservice expects a single header key. Duplicate headers are ending up in a code path that throws instead of returning 4xx. Need quick mitigation and a fix.
alex-platform: Short-term mitigation: normalize tenant header at the edge (drop duplicates, prefer first value) and increase auth cache TTL to reduce backend load. I'll prepare a small nginx/envoy header rewrite rule to canonicalize headers.
kai-oncall: deploy-bot can we run a canary with header normalization on one front region? Also enable a temporary rate-limit on fanout for embeddings (throttle parallelism to 3).
deploy-bot: rollout started: canary deploy id=canary-20241012-01 target=us-west-2-front-01 config=header-normalize,fanout-throttle. Health checks passing on 3/3 nodes so far.
maya-support: Noted — customer upgraded client to 2.4.1 which they say sometimes sends header twice when proxying. Asking them to stop and we suggested workaround: remove duplicate header.
jon-eng-sre: Action items: 1) alex to push header normalization + fanout throttle canary (in progress). 2) kai monitor auth 5xx and cache hit rate, rollback if any negative impact. 3) devs to patch auth service to return 4xx for unknown tenant instead of throwing 500. 4) support to advise customer to upgrade client and avoid double headers.
maya-support: I'll send ACME a mitigation note and ask them to test canary once deployed. Also opening a ticket ACME-502-2024.
alex-platform: After canary we're seeing auth 5xx down ~92% for the traces we tracked, cache hit rate improved. Will schedule a follow-up to harden auth code-path.
kai-oncall: Keeping monitoring on for next 6 hours, will escalate if we see repeat.
maya-support: Closing this thread for now — will update when ACME confirms. :white_check_mark:
